title: AI Agents
summary: Systems where models choose their next action, use tools, keep state, recover from failures and collaborate with other agents.
outcome: Build a real agent that combines planning, tools, state, failure recovery and controlled autonomy, not just an LLM in a loop.

project.title: Production-Style Agent
deliverables: Pick one: research agent (planner → researcher → analyst → writer), MCP server + agent for a real service, or a coding/data agent with sandboxed execution
At least one human approval point for consequential actions
Built in one agent framework, with the underlying loop explained from first principles

modules.title: What is an agent?

topics.d: Goal, decide, act, observe, repeat, finish.

topics.t: Call vs chain vs workflow vs agent
topics.d: Distinguished by who decides the next step.
Open-ended, multi-step tasks with unpredictable paths.
Deterministic flows are simpler, cheaper and more reliable.
Model, instructions, tools, state/memory, loop and stopping conditions.

modules.outcome: Decide whether a problem genuinely needs an agent.

modules.title: ReAct, planning & reflection

topics.d: Alternate reasoning about an action and taking it.

topics.t: Writing the loop by hand first
topics.d: A manual agent loop before any framework.
Incremental execution vs upfront planning.
Split goals and update plans as information arrives.
Review and correct when actions fail.
Max steps and guards against repetition.
Planning and reflection add latency and cost.

modules.outcome: Build an agent that solves a multi-step task without a hard-coded path.

modules.title: Tools for agents

topics.t: From tool calling to agentic tool use
topics.d: The model repeatedly chooses among capabilities.
Clear names, schemas, typed args, useful outputs and errors.
Raising accuracy of tool choice and argument values.
Dependent, concurrent and repeated invocations.
Retry, recover or pick an alternative.
Keep results from flooding the context.
Confirmation and permission checks for risky actions.

modules.outcome: Give an agent useful capabilities without uncontrolled access.

modules.title: MCP (Model Context Protocol)

topics.d: A standard way to connect AI apps to tools, resources and prompts.
The architecture and each component's job.
Tool calling requests actions; MCP standardizes how capabilities are exposed.
Expose tools/resources from a database, filesystem, SaaS app or API.
Capabilities, errors, stdio/HTTP transports and authentication.
An MCP client connected to one or more servers.
Trust boundaries and the risk of untrusted servers.

modules.outcome: Build a reusable MCP integration that exposes a real system to AI apps.

modules.title: Memory basics

topics.d: Distinguishing these four ideas.
Information kept within a conversation or task.
Persistent or retrieval-backed memory across sessions.
Facts, preferences and outcomes rather than every message.
Fetch memories on demand instead of injecting everything.
Basic memory operations.
Managing growing conversations.
Deeper offloading lives in Context Engineering.

modules.outcome: Build an agent that remembers relevant information during and across sessions.

modules.title: Multi-agent architectures

topics.d: Different tools, instructions, models, permissions or expertise.
Overview of multi-agent topologies.
A coordinator delegates to workers.
Agents pass work along in order.
Specialists work on subtasks concurrently.
Multi-level supervision.
Decompose and delegate to specialists.
Sharing context and combining results.
Retries, reassignment and escalation.

topics.t: What goes wrong with many agents
topics.d: Duplication, coordination overhead, context growth, latency and cost.
A2A connects agents to agents; MCP connects agents to tools.

topics.t: When one strong agent is better
topics.d: One capable agent with several tools often wins.

modules.outcome: Use multi-agent designs only when specialization justifies the complexity.

modules.title: Building agents with LangGraph

topics.d: Low-level runtime for long-running, stateful agents.
Modeling execution as a graph.
Nodes for model calls, tools, processing and decisions.
Choosing the next step dynamically.
Repeated tool use and iterative execution.
Saving execution state to survive interruptions.
Continue from a checkpoint rather than restarting.
Pause for approval or intervention.
Understand why a path was taken.

topics.t: When a graph beats a loop
topics.d: When explicit graphs give more control.

modules.outcome: Build a controllable, stateful, resumable agent with explicit execution logic.

modules.title: Sandboxed execution

topics.t: Why generated code must not run in-process
topics.d: Keep generated code out of the production app.
Running code in isolated environments.
Limit filesystem, network, credentials, runtime and compute.
Collect stdout, stderr, files and errors; return only what is needed.
Limit the damage executable actions can do.

modules.outcome: Give an agent code execution without exposing the host.

modules.title: Agent reliability, UX & failure recovery

topics.d: Wrong tools, bad args, loops, incomplete plans and context growth.
Limits on steps, time, retries and spend.
Retries that do not repeat side effects.
Enough saved state to continue after interruption.
Alternatives and handoff when the agent cannot proceed safely.
Show current task, actions, results and approvals.
User control over long-running work.
Clear execution without leaking private reasoning.

modules.outcome: Build agents that fail predictably, recover gracefully and keep users in control.

modules.title: Agent frameworks & libraries

topics.d: Implement one small agent across frameworks.
Graph-based, stateful orchestration with persistence and HITL.
Google's open-source agent framework with sessions, tools and A2A.
Crews for collaborating agents and Flows for controlled workflows.
Agents, Teams and Workflows plus a production runtime.
Code-first agents with tools, handoffs, guardrails and tracing.
Abstraction, control, state, multi-agent, MCP/A2A, observability and flexibility.

modules.outcome: Choose an agent framework by architecture rather than popularity.

modules.title: Capstone: Build a Production-Style Agent

topics.d: Research agent, MCP-powered agent or coding/data agent.
3+ tools, multi-step execution, state, stopping, recovery, logs, an approval point and one framework explained.

modules.outcome: A real agent showing planning, tools, state, recovery and controlled autonomy.
